To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reduced tissue NE content in the atria and ventricles of cardiomyopathic Syrian hamsters is mediated by different cellular mechanisms.

the NE depletion in the cardiomyopathic hamster atria is mediated by different mechanism than the NE depletion in ventricles, that the NE depletion and the decrease of D beta H are not correlated, and that the decrease of D bH and increase of ANF are not correlated.
the atria of cardiomyopathic Syrian hamsters exhibit reduced tissue norepihnephrine content and dopamine-beta-hydoxylase activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the relationship between the catecholamine and ANF content of the atria and ventricles of cardiomyopathic animals, as well as with the relationship between catecholamine content and tissue dopamine-beta-hydroxlase activity.
the relationship between catecholamines, their synthetic enzyme dopamine-beta-hydro-xylase and atrio-ventricular ANF content in a hamster model of cardiomyopathy.
the role of the sympathetic nervous system in the development of heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the decreased ANF content in the atria is not related to the reduced D beta H activity, but rather to the decreased NE content in the atrial tissue.
the ANF concentration in cardiomyopathic hamster ventricles is not a simple reflection of the tissue NE or D beta H content.
, although the atrial and ventricle ANF levels are markedly different, there is a lack of correlation with the tissue CA content or D beta H activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cardiomyopathic hamster heart is a unique model for the study of cardiac ANF.

in cardiomyopathic hamster hearts, the ventricular ANF concentration is not related to the ventricular NE content but is inversely correlated to the ventricular D beta H activity, whereas the atrial ANF concentration is related to the atrial NE content but not to the atrial D beta H activity.
the NE depletion and D beta H activity are not related in the atria, and the NE depletion is not related to D beta H activity, or to ANF concentrations in the ventriclles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NE depletion in the atria and ventricles of cardiomyopathic hearts is mediated by different pathways, and this is not related to D beta H activity.
, in cardiomyopathic hamster, the atrial ANF concentration is not related to the atrial catecholamine content, nor to the D beta H activity.
the atria and ventricles of cardiomyopathic animals are not functionally similar, and the atria are more sensitive to the effects of the disease than the ventricles.
